description:
FILED by Fable 2026-10-06 on the USER`s word ("if you think it can be a win, please log it for later analysis"), from reading the emission of brian d foy`s `print rand 5, sin 4, rand sin 1, 2, 3;`:

  (p-print (p-list-ctx (p-rand 5)) (p-list-ctx (p-sin 4)) (p-list-ctx (p-rand (p-sin 1))) 2 3)

WHERE.  Pl/ExprToCL.pm, the end of the funcall context rule (~line 3001 at main 0d31ef9d): `return $ctx == LIST_CTX ? Pl::CLForm::ctx_bind(`t`, $call) : $call;` -- the fallback for every built-in that is NOT in %WANTARRAY_SENSITIVE (line 222).  The table`s members are bound in BOTH contexts just above it; the fallback binds everything else in list context only.  The table`s own comment states the INVARIANT "this set must list EVERY runtime builtin that branches on *wantarray*" -- if that holds, the fallback bind is redundant for every built-in it reaches.  In a SCALAR slot the same call is already emitted bare (`my $x = rand 5` -> `(p-my-= $x (p-rand 5))`).

HOW COMMON.  Every built-in call written as an ARGUMENT is in a list slot: `f(length $s)`, `push @a, lc $x`, `print uc $s`, `@r = (abs $i, int $i)`, a `return` list.

MEASURED (the cheap discriminating measurement; quiet-ish box, best of 5, twice, SBCL on the cached core):
  my $s = "hello world"; my $t = 0; my @keep;  sub f { $_[0] }
  for my $i (1 .. 4_000_000) { $t += f(length $s); $t += f(ord $s); @keep = (abs $i, int $i, lc $s); }
  emitted as-is (5 wraps per iteration):   0.651 s / 0.652 s
  the 5 wraps removed BY HAND in the .lisp: 0.612 s / 0.627 s      (perl: 0.84 s)
  = 25-39 ms over 20 M removed binds = ~1.2-2 ns per wrap; 4-6 % of this loop, whose every statement carries one.  A real program will show far less.  So: a SMALL win in time, plus Target B value -- docs/generated-cl-ir-review.md 3.5 counts the context binds as the loudest thing in the emitted file (7-17 per 100 lines).

BEFORE DOING IT (not taken, each is minutes to an hour):
  1. VERIFY THE INVARIANT: list every function in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp (and the three transpiled artifacts) that reads *wantarray*, and compare with %WANTARRAY_SENSITIVE + the non-funcall node types (readline, glob, sort/map/grep, do FILE).  A built-in that reads it and is missing from the table is passing today only because of this fallback.
  2. COUNT IT: how many fallback binds the bench board and the everyday corpus emit, and around which built-ins (an env-switched counter at the site, or a grep of the emission against the table).
  3. CALLBACKS: a built-in outside the table can still run USER code (an overload handler under `abs $obj`, a tie FETCH).  With the bind gone that code sees the ENCLOSING sub`s context in a list slot -- which is what it already sees in a scalar slot today.  Probe what perl gives a handler (`wantarray` inside an overload sub / FETCH) before deciding it does not matter.
  4. THE BAR: it is an emission change across most of the corpus (the `join` note at ~2967 measured 12 corpus files for join`s bind alone) -> corpus-diff read per file, generation bump, artifacts rebuilt, full sweep + companion --quick, the bench board before/after.

SHAPE OF THE FIX if the invariant holds: delete the fallback (or keep a short NEGATIVE list if step 1 finds built-ins that need it and do not belong in the table).  Per-builtin "context-blind" lists are the wrong direction -- the table of the sensitive ones already exists (rule 11).

PRIORITY: perf is prioritised by MEASURED gain (USER s499) -- this one is small; a filler for a perf round, after #2770-#2773.

USER 2026-10-06 (s510): "Please create a job for doing careful analysis of this before doing it - nicer and more readable CL is a good thing. Don't make it highly prioritized."  => THE JOB is `briefs-and-rules-for-claude-subagents/s510/analysis-2775-prompt.md` (label a2775; analysis only, nothing under Pl/ cl/ lib/ committed; its report = docs/ctx-bind-fallback-analysis-s510.md, sections A-F: is the table complete / who runs user code from inside a built-in / how much of the emission it is / a trial removal through the gate, the sweep and everyday / the run-time gain with a control band / the reader's before-after).  It takes a slot AFTER the three checkpointed batches (s507c PART TWO, s508a, s507p).  NOTHING is changed in the compiler before the reviewing session has ruled on that report; readability of the generated CL counts as a reason to do it, beside the small speed gain.
subject: LOW PRIORITY, ANALYSIS FIRST (USER 2026-10-06) -- PERF + IR noise (measured SMALL, for later analysis -- USER 2026-10-06): a built-in call in a LIST slot always gets `(p-list-ctx ...)`, also when the built-in never reads *wantarray* (rand sin length ord abs int lc ...) -- ~1.5 ns per call, 4-6 % on a loop dense with them
